title: The Silent Valley
author: Haruo Minase
abstract: A surveyor is sent to map a mountain valley whose villagers have agreed, generations ago, never to speak above a whisper. As the snow closes the pass he begins to understand what the silence is protecting — and what it has cost. Minase’s spare first novel is set here in the original quarto, with eleven tipped-in woodcut plates.

title: An Atlas of Lost Weather
author: Ilse Varga
abstract: Forty-one short essays, each describing a kind of weather that no longer occurs: the brown fogs of river cities, the dry lightning of a drained marsh, a wind that once had a name. Varga writes as a meteorologist and a mourner at once. Bound with the folding isobar chart intact.

title: The Blue Hour
author: Margit Halloran
abstract: Over a single dusk in a harbour town, a night-telephone operator connects six calls that should never have reached one another. Halloran’s novella unfolds in real time, minute by minute, until the street lamps come on. An unusually clean copy in the publisher’s indigo cloth.

title: Cartographer of Moths
author: Teodor Brandt
abstract: Part field journal, part confession: an amateur lepidopterist spends thirty summers charting the night flights of moths across one fjord, and slowly realises the map he is drawing is of his own family. Illustrated throughout with the author’s wing diagrams.

title: River of Salt
author: Elias Okonkwo-Reed
abstract: Three brothers inherit a salt works on an estuary that is moving inland a little further every year. A family saga told against the tide tables, where every chapter opens with the day’s high-water mark. The scarce first state, with the misprinted tide chart on page 9.

title: The Glass Orchard
author: Sayo Kirishima
abstract: A sequence of sixty-four prose poems written in a greenhouse through one winter, each pane of glass a page. Kirishima counts frost, breath and pears with the same instrument. Printed letterpress on Echizen paper; this copy retains the glassine wrapper.

title: Winter Arithmetic
author: Anders Lindqvist
abstract: A schoolteacher on a northern island keeps the ledger for a community that pays its debts in firewood, herring and favours. When the ice comes early, the sums stop balancing. A quiet, exact novel about what people owe each other when nothing else can be counted on.

title: Noon in Ashes
author: Corwin Mackery
abstract: After a fire takes the grasslands, a drover and a telegraph clerk cross the burn on foot with a single mule, following a wire that may no longer lead anywhere. Mackery strips the western down to light, distance and thirst. Publisher’s grey cloth with the vermilion sun device.

title: Night Ferry to Otaru
author: Reiko Asahina
abstract: Nine passengers, one overnight crossing, and a purser who has been asked to deliver a letter to someone on board without being told to whom. Asahina’s chamber novel is as much about the sound of the engine as the people above it. With the fold-out deck plan.

title: Thirteen Quiet Rooms
author: Beatrix Aldous
abstract: Thirteen stories, each confined to a single room: a waiting room, a darkroom, a room let by the week. Aldous allows nothing to happen and makes it unbearable. One of 250 copies signed by the author on the limitation leaf.

title: The Paper Tide
author: Lucien Ferrand
abstract: An archivist in a port city discovers that the municipal records are being quietly rewritten, one shipping manifest at a time, and decides to keep a second, secret archive in the margins of unsold novels. A comedy of filing that turns, very slowly, into a thriller.

title: A Lantern for the Drowned
author: Tomás Echeverri
abstract: Each year a fishing town lights one lantern for every boat that did not come back. The year the lamplighter’s own son is lost, she refuses, and the harbour goes dark. Echeverri’s last novel, and his most generous. Deep teal cloth, top edge stained ochre.
